text.p: Lithuania's finance minister says that the government's targets for revenue collection will be met this year.
"If all the measures are taken that have been approved by the government, we should reach our targets for revenue collection this year," Algirdas Shemeta told Reuters in an interview.
The budget passed by parliament in December calls for a deficit of almost 700 million litas.
The government has vowed to meet all of its budgetary targets and has declared war on tax evasion, which is considered to be rife.

"We were a bit behind in revenue collection in January and the first half of February, and now we are falling just short of target," Shemeta said. "Of course, it will require some effort to collect the money we missed in that period."
Shemeta said that he did not expect a big fall or rise in the country's domestic borrowing costs.
"I think that the local Treasury bill market has stabilized...there will no big movements in either direction," he said.
The average yield on 91-day government paper rose at Monday's auction to 11.37 percent from 10.70 percent.
